JUDGMENT

By this judgment this Tribunal shall decide the petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 01.05.2022 at about 6.40am petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing No.KA-05-KR-3076 ridden by one Prajwal from west of chord main road, Chandra layout junction towards Bapujinagar and while so proceeding near Attiguppe Bus stop, Prajwal drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner with high speed and suddenly applied brake, due to which both fell down from the motorcycle and petitioner sustained fracture shaft of tibia and other injuries all over the body.
Immediately he was shifted to Vijayanagar hospital, Bangalore and admitted as inpatient and underwent treatment from 01.05.2022 to (SCCH-12) 3 MVC. No.2849/2022 04.05.2022.
That he has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. It is further stated in the petition that prior to accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was a Govt.Employee and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to the accident he has lost his income and underwent mental agony and suffering.
That accidental injuries have caused permanent disability to the petitioner.

The Byatarayanapura Traffic Police have registered case in Crime No.63/2022 against the rider of said vehicle and after investigation, they have filed the charge sheet against the said rider for the offence p/u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
The 1 st respondent is the owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of said vehicle.
Hence, both are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds, he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 is served.
He remained absent before the court hence he is placed exparte.
2 nd respondent appeared through counsel and filed written statement and contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
That he has not issued any motor policy of insurance in favour of 1 st respondent in respect of Motor cycle bearing no.KA-05-KR-3076 covering third party risk.
Hence petition against this respondent does not survive for consideration and requires to be dismissed.
That the policy number mentioned in the cause title of the petition is issued covering own damages only that is stand alone policy.
That the 3rd party cover to Motor cycle bearing no.KA-05-KR-3076 is (SCCH-12) 4 MVC. No.2849/2022 i s s u e d b y o n e M / s I C I C I L o m b a r d G e n .
I n s .
C o . L t d u n d e r m o t o r p o l i c y no.3005201085475600000001303 valid from 30.01.2020 to 29.01.025 covering the date of accident.
He denied all other averments of plaint.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

2 5.
Thereafter petitioner filed application to implead ICICI Lombard Ins. Company as additional respondent and the said application came to be allowed.

The said insurance company has been numbered as respondent no.3.
6.
3rd respondent insurance company filed written statement denying the petition averments.
Further it contended that it also has not issued the policy in respect of Motor cycle bearing no.KA-05-KR-3076.
That if at all any policy is issued, the liability of this respondent is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance.
That the said motor cycle was not at all involved in the accident and same has been implicated in the alleged accident by colluding with the owner.
That the owner of the vehicle has not submitted the claim form and other documents like RC, DL etc for verification.
That the police have not informed the alleged accident to the concerned jurisdictional court and also to this respondent.
That the owner and police have not complied the mandatory provision of Motor Vehicle Act.
That the rider of motor cycle rode the same without having a valid and effective driving license which is in contravention of the policy condition and also the Motor Vehicle Act.
Manner of accident alleged by the petitioner is denied.
Age, occupation, physical disability and medical expenses alleged are denied.
On (SCCH-12) 5 MVC. No.2849/2022 all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.

The learned counsel for 3rd respondent has relied upon Judgment in CMA No.2093/2023 dt. 12.12.2024 The Hon'ble High Court of Madras between Pula Shanmjugam and another V/s Yugender Ravellah and others.

sentences.text: 7. On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are framed:-

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that 01.05.2022 at about 6.40 am when petitioner was traveling on two wheeler bearing reg.no.KA- 05-KR-3076 as pillion rider driven by one Prajwal on West of Cord Road, Chandra Layout Junction towards Babujinagara
, said Prajwal rode the said vehicle in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed suddenly applied brake due to which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability, if any?
3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves that he issued OD policy and it will not cover the risk alleged in the petition?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5.
What Order or Award?
8. To prove his case, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through him Ex.P.1 to P.11 documents are marked.
One Naveen Kumar T.B. Medical Record Executive, (SCCH-12) 6 MVC. No.2849/2022 Vijayanagar hospital is examined as P.W.2.
Through him Ex.P.12 to 16 Shivamurthy.
L vs Prajwal.S

on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123808530/
3 documents are marked.
The representative of 2 nd respondent company got examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.R.1 and 2 documents are marked.
Legal Manager of 3rd respondent got examined as R.W.2 and through him Ex.R.3 is marked and respondent side evidence is closed.
9. Heard learned counsel for both sides.
2nd respondent filed written arguments.
Perused the records.

10. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and arguments of both sides, I answer the above issues as follows: -
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.5: As per final order,
 for the following;
 REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1 : It is the case of the petitioner he sustained injuries due to the accident caused by bike rider who is none other than his son.
It is stated that petitioner was pillion rider and his son was riding the bike.
His son is respondent no.1, who is exparte.
To show that petitioner sustained injuries due to RTA, petitioner filed affidavit and got examined as P.W.1.
In his affidavit he reiterated petition averments.
He relied upon FIR, first information, spot panchanama, spot sketch, IMV report, Wound certificate and final report.
On perusal of those (SCCH-12) 7 MVC. No.2849/2022 documents it can be seen that petitioner himself is the first informant.
After 2 days of the accident first information is given and FIR is registered on the basis of statement given before doctor at Vijayanagar hospital.
It is stated that since the petitioner was taking treatment at the hospital there is delay in filing the complaint.
The delay is only 2 days.
It requires to be ignored in view of fracture of leg caused to petitioner.
Spot panchanama was conducted on the next day of the FIR.
It is a 2 lane main road where the accident has taken place and there is center median and also there are metro pillars and there is also footpath on both sides.
As per the rough sketch on the left side of the road accident has taken place near the junction.
The time of the accident is 6.40 am.
There is no dispute as to visibility of the vehicle.
As per the IMV report rear left side body and rear left side foot scratched.
As per the wound certificate petitioner has sustained fracture of right tibia and swelling of right ankle.
As per the charge sheet the rider of bike i.e., R-1 is found to be negligent and charge sheet is filed against him.
The said charge sheet and final report are not questioned by the bike rider-cum- owner.
In Ex.P.14 MLC register extract it is mentioned as self fall from 2 wheeler near Attiguppe and informant is son.
In the police intimation which is sent on the same day of the accident I is mentioned as fall from 2 wheeler.
Since there are no 2 vehicles involved in the accident and petitioner being pillion rider and his son riding the bike, it is fall from the bike.
In the evidence P.W.1 stated that he was taking drop from his son and denied petitioner himself was riding the bike.
Though negligence of the petitioner and he himself riding the bike is contended by (SCCH-12) 8 MVC. No.2849/2022 the 3rd respondent no independent evidence is placed in that regard.

Hence, in the opinion of this court on the basis of oral and documentary evidence petitioner has proved that rider of 2 wheeler bearing Shivamurthy.L vs Prajwal.S on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123808530/
4 no.KA-05-KR-3076 was rash and negligent in riding the vehicle.
Accordingly, I answer this issue in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE NO.2 :
To prove his age petitioner has produced aadhaar card at Ex.P.10 which shows his date of birth as 12.07.1968.
Accident took place on 01.05.2022.
He was aged 53 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 53 years at the time of accident.
13. In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was a Govt. employee and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
To prove this fact he has not produced document.
Hence notional income has to be considered.
The accident took place in the year 2022.
Therefore monthly income of the petitioner is held as Rs.15,500/-.
In respect of permanent disability petitioner has not led any evidence.
Therefore, it is held that there is no functional disability affecting the income of petitioner.
Accordingly this issue is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.3:
According to 2nd respondent he has issued only O.D policy which will not cover the risk of 3rd party.
To prove this fact he got authorized representative as R.W.1 and the copy of policy is produced at Ex.R.2.
In the chief examination R.W.1 reiterated the similar fact.
In Ex.R.2 it is mentioned that it is stand alone 2 wheeler own damage policy covering from 07.05.2021 to 06.05.2022.

The said policy covers (SCCH-12) 9 MVC. No.2849/2022 own damage to vehicle,
electronic accessories.
The same will not cover 3rd party risks.
In the cross examination of R.W.1 by 3 rd respondent it is categorically mentioned by the R.W.1 that 3 rd party claim is not included in O.D policy.
To contradict the same, no evidence is placed.
Therefore 2nd respondent has proved that the policy issued by him will not cover 3 rd party risks.
Hence, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.4: In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In the cross examination of R.W.2 who is legal manager of 3rd respondent insurance company, he has stated that the policy issued by 3rd respondent is covering 3rd party risks for 5 years and O.D policy for 1 year which is bundled policy.
There is no change of policy conditions after the issuance of policy.
After admitting the existence of policy, R.W.2 stated that for pillion rider the risk is not covered in the 2 nd year of insurance, but no such mention is made in the policy.

Counsel for 3rd respondent relied upon judgment in CMA No.2093/2023 dt. 12.12.2024 The Hon'ble High Court of Madras between Pula Shanmjugam and another V/s Yugender Ravellah and others in which it is held that insurer has to pay extra premium to cover the pillion rider.

entities.text: Pula Shanmjugam and another V/s Yugender Ravellah and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No such extra payment has been paid by the owner extending the insurance company's liability to pillion rider who was deceased in the said case and therefore it is held that insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to petitioners in that case.
But, in the present case as per Ex.R.3 policy on the right side in which policy number is mentioned that tenure is shown (SCCH-12) 10 MVC. No.2849/2022 as own damage 1 year and third party 5 years.
It is necessary to notice that, 3rd respondent has issued 3rd party coverage policy and petition herein being pillion rider is 3 rd party to the policy of insurance between R-1 and R-3.
Therefore, 3 rd respondent will have to be made responsible to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to petitioner and the aforesaid judgment is not applicable to the present case.

Hence, the quantum of Shivamurthy.L vs Prajwal.S on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123808530/
5 compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced IP medical bill of Vijayanagar hospital at Ex.P.11 petitioner has paid Rs.1,68,575/- towards medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
The same is disputed as reimbursed as he is Govt. employee.
But he denied the same.
No evidence is placed to prove reimbursement of bill.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,68,575/-.
(ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was admitted in Vijayanagar hospital from 01.05.2022 to 04.05.2022.
No discharge summary is produced showing his inpatient period but case sheet is produced at Ex.P.15 which shows that petitioner was admitted as inpatient in the said hospital for 4 days.

Considering the cost of living, food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded,
Rs.500/- x 04 days = Rs.2,000/-it will meet the ends of justice.
(iii) Attendant charges: The petitioner sustained one grievous injury of tibia and one simple injury and took treatment at Vijayanagar hospital, Bangalore.
Someone must have taken care of the petitioner during his treatment period.
Hence, attendant charges of Rs.2,000/- is awarded.
(SCCH-12) 11 MVC. No.2849/2022 (iv) Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.15,500/-.
He underwent surgery for right tibia.

But he being Govt.
employee loss of his salary for the laid up period is not established by evidence.
Therefore, there is no ground to compensation for loss of income during laid up period.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(v) Conveyance charges:
Petitioner has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Considering the same, this court is of the opinion that amount of Rs.3,000/- shall be awarded as conveyance charges.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability : Petitioner has not examined doctor.
There is no evidence regarding physical disability.
As per the findings given above, there is no functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(vii) For Future medical expenses: There is no evidence to show that there is need of future medical treatment in respect of the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained fracture of right tibia and swelling of right ankle.
He underwent surgery at hospital and suffered pain and agony.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- .

Shivamurthy.L vs Prajwal.S on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123808530/
6
(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life : There is no evidence of doctor to show that grievous injury has (SCCH-12) 12 MVC. No.2849/2022 affected the normal life of the petitioner.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded under this head.
(x) Loss of future prospect:

As per the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme court, even in injury cases,
loss of future prospect has to be considered.
But in the present case, the on going through the evidence and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner there is no chance of loss of future prospect.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.

Medical expenses 1,68,575 /-
ii. Food and nourishment 2,000/-
iii Attendant charges 2,000/-
iv. Loss of income during laid up Nil  period v. Conveyance charges 3,000/-

vi . Loss of income due to disability Nil vii Future medical expenses Nil viii Pain and sufferings 30,000/-
ix. Physical discomfort and loss of Nil  amenities of life x. Loss of future prospects
In view of above reasons, 3rd respondent insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
16. ISSUE NO.5 : In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following;
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

Shivamurthy.L vs Prajwal.S on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123808530/
7
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,05,575/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment.

Respondent no.3 insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest before this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire amount on his proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

iv. Loss of income during laid up Nil  period v. Conveyance charges 3,000/-
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
16. ISSUE NO.5 : In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following;
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,05,575/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment.

Respondent no.3 insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest before this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of entire amount on his proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
